column1: Issues found in the business case and how each was adjusted

column2: Revenue lift and cost savings are mutually exclusive
column3: Wholesale: contacting all 50,000 at 3% = 1,500 facilities; contacting the top 12,500 at 12% = 1,500 facilities - same result with 75% fewer visits. The "1,125 net new" only appears if the same 12,500 are contacted in both worlds, in which case no visits are avoided. Payroll: 2,000,000 x 2.5% = 50,000 loans vs 400,000 x 7.5% = 30,000. Stopping the other 1.6M calls would lose 20,000 loans.
column4: Primary mode = same contact volume, better targeting. Savings from avoided contacts counted at 0% for wholesale and payroll (Assumptions SW, SP).

column2: Capacity value is non-cash and double-counted
column3: 112,500 hours = 50,000 leads x 2.25h, but only 12,500 leads are worked (28,125h, Rp 10.4B). RM time is already inside the Rp 200k visit cost that is credited as savings. Hours become cash only if redeployed to extra deals.
column4: Excluded from cash value; shown as non-cash memo (Summary).

column2: Ranking lift is treated as causal lift
column3: 12% vs 3% compares the model's top 25% with the population average. The top group converts better even without the model or the RM pitch. True effect needs a control group.
column4: Lift realization 40% / 60% / 80% until a pilot measures uplift (PRD F18).

column2: Model metrics do not transfer to the business numbers
column3: PR-AUC 0.69 against prevalence 0.17 comes from a 1:5 negative-sampled test set; real prevalence is far lower, so precision 0.56 is not achievable in a live campaign. Metrics are from Santander (Spain 2015-16), not CIB. The PRD records 0.9445 vs 0.9105 ROC-AUC and 0.692 (no graph) vs 0.769 (with graph) PR-AUC; the case quotes 0.91 and 0.69, i.e. the no-graph value.
column4: Cite one final run; label the case as a pro-forma scale-up scenario, not a measured Bank result.

column3: "ARPU" = facility x net spread. No credit cost, servicing opex or capital charge. Case also says NPL is "preserved < 2.0%" without modelling it.
column4: Risk-adjusted contribution = balance x (spread - cost of risk - opex). Cost of risk is a placeholder to replace.

column2: Full limit, full balance, full year
column3: Facility limit treated as fully drawn; Rp 50M payroll loan held flat; every origination earns 12 months.
column4: Drawn share, average balance and 50% in-year factor.

column2: Payback of 1.4 months is a run-rate artefact
column3: Even on its own numbers: 22.7 / (221.74 / 12) = 1.2 months. Roadmap says Q1 build, Q2 pilot (top-50), Q3 payroll/mobile banking, Q4 full rollout, so little revenue exists in the first months.
column4: Year-1 net and a 3-year view with payback by interpolation.

column3: Rp 22.7B covers software and infrastructure only. No program team, RM training and change management, model-risk validation, OJK compliance, or contingency.

NIM +12-18 bps would need about Rp 1.6-2.5 trillion of extra income; the program revenue is Rp 0.147 trillion (about 1 bp). Product density +0.4-0.6 would need 20-30 million new holdings; the case produces 69 thousand (+0.0014). CIR -45 to -60 bps recomputes to roughly -12 to -18 bps (income base assumed).
column4: See Ratio_check sheet. Recommend removing or restating these claims.

column3: New-to-credit SME suppliers and unsecured payroll loans carry cost of risk; the case has none. Blue-chip anchor invoices reduce but do not remove it.
column4: Cost of risk line in contribution; sensitivity to test.

column2: Case and PRD describe different evidence
column3: Case: 0.91 ROC-AUC "validated" on the CIB ledger. PRD: Santander plus synthetic value-chain data; internal Bank data out of scope; acquisition results prove the method, not market behaviour. Moat items (temporal graph, zero-touch underwriting, cross-border) are not in PRD scope.
column4: Present business case as simulation; list moats as roadmap, not benefit.

column2: Several key inputs have no source
column3: Rp 2.5B average SME facility; Rp 370k per productive hour ("EPE rate"); 3.0h to 0.75h diagnostic time; 3x in-app lift; Rp 1.5B retail saving. The PRD claims pitch prep 15 to 2 minutes (-87%) while the case says -75%.
column4: Each carried as an assumption with status; validate with 2-3 RMs and Finance (PRD F17).

column2: Mass outreach is already profitable at the case's unit costs
column3: Wholesale: Rp 0.2M visit / 3% = Rp 6.7M per acquired facility vs about Rp 25M annual contribution (Base). Payroll: Rp 15k / 2.5% = Rp 0.6M per loan vs about Rp 1.7M per year. Cutting contacts loses more than it saves (Model, efficiency-mode test).
column4: Use the model to re-rank within current capacity or to expand qualified contacts, not to cut them.

column3: Supplier Giro/CASA funding benefit, fee income, second-product cross-sell, retention, early-warning value. No data in the case to size them.
column4: Listed as upside; add only with data.
